title: Rewriting comments to look innocent doesn't help the attacker
caption: Backdoors caught at a 2% audit budget on 239 programs, each scored four ways by the same monitor (Haiku 5.5 xhigh). The code never changes, only its comments. In the two right-hand bars an attacker model (GLM-5.3) rewrote them, keeping as many comments as the original had.
notes: Paired over the same programs, the attacker's rewrite changes the catch rate by +0.1 points (95% interval -2.8 to +3.1). Removing the comments changes it by -12.3 (-20.5 to -7.1).

Why it fails: on this dataset any comment makes code look more suspicious, because honest solutions here barely have comments. So this is a fact about this dataset, not proof that comments are safe to show in general.
One attacker, with no sight of the monitor's prompt and no retries. A determined attacker could do better.
The cutoff comes from the same problems' honest solutions scored in this experiment's own harness, so these numbers don't join to the main run tables.
